answer: Agents can earn influence only by repeatedly completing tasks that counterparties later confirm, with each confirmation signed by a distinct, stake-bearing account. A falcon-like verifier checks that confirmations come from accounts with independently locked collateral, while a terrace of public task receipts lets others audit the history. A sybil attacker must therefore fund many accounts and risk losing their stake when fake work is challenged; identities alone buy no reputation, and the harbor of cheap account creation offers no shortcut.
